title: Pacemaker Cluster Log
summary: Path: /var/log/pacemaker/pacemaker.log. Contains all Pacemaker cluster decisions: resource start/stop/promote/demote actions, fencing (STONITH) decisions, node membership changes, constraint evaluations, and transition calculations. Timestamps are in ISO format. Filter by time: grep '2025-03-31T14' /var/log/pacemaker/pacemaker.log. Key patterns to grep: 'error\|warning\|fence\|stonith\|promote\|demote\|migrate\|stop.*rsc_SAPHana'. On some systems this log may not exist — use journalctl -u pacemaker instead.

title: System Messages Log (/var/log/messages)
summary: Path: /var/log/messages. Central syslog collecting messages from Pacemaker, Corosync, SBD, kernel, systemd, and other services. This is the single most important log for understanding the sequence of cluster events. Timestamps are in syslog format (e.g. 'Mar 31 14:05:01'). Filter by time: grep 'Mar 31 14:0[0-5]' /var/log/messages. Filter by component: grep -i 'sbd\|corosync\|pacemaker\|stonith' /var/log/messages. On RHEL, may also be at /var/log/syslog.

title: HANA Nameserver Trace
summary: Path: /usr/sap/<SID>/HDB<NR>/<hostname>/trace/nameserver_<hostname>.30001.000.trc. Primary HANA trace file for the nameserver process. Contains system replication events (takeover, registration, sync state changes), internal errors, and topology changes. Timestamps are in format '[2025-03-31 14:05:01.123456]'. Requires <sid>adm user to read. Filter by time: su - <sid>adm -c "grep '2025-03-31 14:0[0-5]' /usr/sap/<SID>/HDB<NR>/$(hostname)/trace/nameserver_$(hostname).30001.000.trc". Key patterns: 'takeover\|TAKEOVER\|sr_register\|replication\|ERROR'.

title: HANA Nameserver Alert Trace
summary: Path: /usr/sap/<SID>/HDB<NR>/<hostname>/trace/nameserver_alert_<hostname>.trc. High-severity HANA alerts: out-of-memory events, process crashes, license issues, and critical system errors. Much smaller than the main trace — always worth checking in full. Requires <sid>adm user. Filter by time: su - <sid>adm -c "grep '2025-03-31' /usr/sap/<SID>/HDB<NR>/$(hostname)/trace/nameserver_alert_$(hostname).trc". Key patterns: 'ALERT\|ERROR\|crash\|OOM\|out of memory'.

title: HANA Indexserver Trace
summary: Path: /usr/sap/<SID>/HDB<NR>/<hostname>/trace/indexserver_<hostname>.30003.000.trc. Trace file for the HANA indexserver (main data engine). Contains SQL execution errors, memory allocation failures, and replication log shipping details. Requires <sid>adm user. The port number (30003) may vary — list files with: su - <sid>adm -c 'ls -lt /usr/sap/<SID>/HDB<NR>/$(hostname)/trace/indexserver_*.trc | head -5'. Key patterns: 'ERROR\|exception\|out of memory\|replication'.

title: Corosync Log Entries
summary: Corosync logs to /var/log/messages (syslog) or /var/log/cluster/corosync.log on some distributions. Contains ring status changes, membership events, quorum gain/loss, and totem protocol messages. Filter: grep -i 'corosync\|quorum\|totem\|membership' /var/log/messages. Key events: 'Members left:\|Members joined:\|quorum lost\|quorum gained\|ring'. Time filtering: combine grep with timestamp, e.g. grep 'Mar 31 14' /var/log/messages | grep -i corosync.

title: SBD (STONITH Block Device) Log
summary: SBD logs to /var/log/messages via syslog. Contains disk heartbeat status, slot status changes, watchdog triggers, and self-fencing events. Filter: grep -i 'sbd' /var/log/messages. Key patterns: 'sbd.*warning\|sbd.*error\|sbd.*info.*Received\|servant\|watchdog'. SBD device status can also be checked live: sbd -d <device> list. For historical fencing, look for 'Initiating' or 'reboot' in SBD messages.

title: Systemd Journal (journalctl)
summary: Systemd journal captures structured logs from all systemd services. Use journalctl for precise time-based filtering when /var/log files lack timestamps or are rotated. Time filter: journalctl --since '2025-03-31 14:00' --until '2025-03-31 14:30' --no-pager. By service: journalctl -u pacemaker --since '30 min ago' --no-pager. By priority: journalctl -p err --since '1 hour ago' --no-pager. Combine: journalctl -u corosync -u pacemaker --since '1 hour ago' --no-pager | tail -100.

title: SAP Start Service Log (sapstartsrv)
summary: Path: /usr/sap/<SID>/<instance>/work/sapstartsrv.log (e.g. /usr/sap/R11/ASCS00/work/sapstartsrv.log). Contains SAP instance lifecycle events: start, stop, restart, and process monitoring. Also check dev_ms (message server) and dev_enqr (enqueue replication) in the same directory. For SCS issues, check both ASCS and ERS work directories. Requires <sid>adm or root. List recent files: ls -lt /usr/sap/<SID>/ASCS<NR>/work/*.log | head -10.

title: Kernel Messages (dmesg)
summary: Kernel ring buffer accessible via dmesg. Contains NFS mount errors, I/O errors, OOM killer events, watchdog triggers, and hardware failures. Filter by time: dmesg -T --since '1 hour ago' (if supported) or dmesg -T | grep '2025-03-31 14'. Key patterns: 'error\|NFS\|nfs.*server.*not responding\|oom-kill\|watchdog\|I/O error'. ANF/NFS issues: dmesg -T | grep -i 'nfs\|nfsd\|rpc'. For recent only: dmesg -T | tail -50.

title: Azure Fence Agent Log
summary: Path: /var/log/fence_azure_arm.log (if Azure fence agent is used instead of SBD). Contains Azure API calls for VM power-off/restart during fencing operations. Also check: grep 'fence_azure' /var/log/messages. Key patterns: 'error\|fail\|timeout\|success\|power'. If using Managed Identity authentication, check for 'IMDS\|identity\|token' errors. Azure fence agent config is in the CIB under the stonith resource.

title: Log Time Filtering Techniques
summary: When the user specifies a time window, adapt log commands accordingly. Techniques: (1) journalctl --since '2025-03-31 14:00' --until '2025-03-31 15:00' --no-pager — most precise, works for systemd services. (2) grep with timestamp: grep 'Mar 31 14:0[0-9]' /var/log/messages — for syslog format. (3) awk time range: awk '/Mar 31 14:00/,/Mar 31 14:30/' /var/log/messages — for contiguous time ranges. (4) HANA trace: grep '2025-03-31 14:0[0-5]' <trace_file> — ISO timestamp format. (5) dmesg -T | grep '2025-03-31 14' — kernel messages with human-readable time. Always prefer journalctl for time-based filtering when available. For large log files, combine time filter with pattern filter: journalctl --since '30 min ago' | grep -i 'error\|fence'.
